headline: Approved July meeting minutes with a correction; discussed Greeley Park master plan, forest health, and wading pool repairs.
summary: The committee approved the July minutes with a correction and discussed building a master plan for Greeley Park, including its history and a contested will. Members also reviewed wading pool repair plans, forest health concerns, and agreed to seek a professional forester evaluation before any tree cutting.
decisions: Approved the July meeting minutes with a correction.

decision_evidence.quote: The minutes from July meeting were approved, with a correction acknowledged.

plain_text:
Greeley Park Advisory Committee 
Mines Fall Conference Room 
848 West Hollis Street 
 
 
Date: August 12, 2026 
Call to Order: 5:06PM 
 
Attendees:  
Committee Members Fran Murphy, Stephanie Ballentine, Vicki Donchess, Sue McNamee, Kathy 
Lodi, Lisa Law, Kerry Miller, Richard Smart 
Superintendent Bryan Conant 
Alderman Trish Klee 
Nashua Conservation Commission Will Darby  
Quorum was determined to be present 
Approval of Minutes: The minutes from July meeting were approved, with a correction acknowledged. 
Public Comment: no public attendees or comment 
Issues with email delivery of last month’s minutes were noted, as messages to Richard Smart’s bounced 
and some participants did not receive emails. To resolve this, it was suggested that a sign-in sheet be 
circulated to collect correct email addresses. 
Additional Committee members: There was a discussion about recruiting members from different parts 
of the city to ensure broader representation beyond the North End. 
Communication Rules: A question was raised about the rules for communicating outside of official 
meetings, noting a quorum is seven and that discussions among more than half of that number may be 
restricted.  
Discussion of Greeley Park History and Master Plan: 
 Kathy Lodi researched the Unique Identity and Historical Context of the Park: Greeley Park is seen as a 
distinct gathering space, akin to Frederick Law Olmsted's vision of providing green spaces for city 
workers. The park's land was willed to the city with the stipulation that it must be kept as open public 
space, and no for-profit businesses can be established on the grounds. A copy of the will is considered 
crucial for the Master Plan. The park's history includes tenant farmers, a contested will, an 8-ton boulder 
from Hollis marking old gravesites, and a hidden burial knoll of historical significance. Ways to 
disseminate this info to the interested public was discussed. 
Public Notices and Communication Channels: For park updates, there was a consensus to use the Parks 
and Recreation webpage and the DPW Facebook page. For major items, coordination with the mayor’s 
office for banner notifications will be considered. It was noted that physical signs are also used at 
facilities for important notices like closures.
Master Plan Development: It was again emphasized that all activities, including marketing and forestry 
management, should fall under a comprehensive master plan. Developing this plan is a multi-year 
process, and it was suggested to request FY28 funds for evaluation and planning.  
Matt Sullivan will be invited to the September meeting for an update on the Master Plan's Request for 
Proposal (RFP) and funding status. 
Locating Historical Plans: An effort will be made to locate the original Master Plan for Greeley Park, which 
was once publicly displayed. Potential contacts include Dan Hudson and Mark Sanders in the 
Engineering department, the Planning Department, Public Works, and the historical society. 
Marketing Campaign for Park History: A marketing campaign was proposed to generate public interest in 
the park's history via the city website. The initiative is seen as a way to build support while the master 
plan is developed. 
Facebook Page and Community Engagement: The idea of creating a "Greeley Park Past, Present, Future" 
Facebook page was proposed to educate the community and share updates on committee activities. The 
goal is to build broad community support and promote the park's diverse use by multi-generational and 
multi-ethnic families. 
Pool Status and Repairs: Wading Pool Design Details: The new wading pool will be similar to the original 
in depth and dimensions but will feature an ADA-compliant beach-slope entry and a slightly larger 
concrete deck. The pool area may be raised slightly due to an old well. No drawings or photos were 
available for review. Time line for completion is not currently known. 
Updates are posted on the Parks and Rec page and DPW Facebook. Signs indicating closure and 
reopening plans were to be installed. Centennial Park and another pool were closing on August 14 due to 
lifeguard availability, with one pool remaining open for an additional week. 
Forest Health and Goals: Concerns were raised about dead trees and overall forest health at Greeley 
Park. The primary goal is to improve safety, reduce fire risk, and allow sunlight for regeneration by first 
cleaning the forest floor of dead debris before any tree cutting is considered. The committee has not 
decided on harvesting live trees. There is agreement to seek a professional evaluation from a licensed 
forester and to explore the UNH Cooperative Extension for input, with a need to confirm any cost for their 
services. Any outreach and walkthroughs will be coordinated with DPW/BPW, and public notice may be 
required if a quorum of the committee attends. 
Sustainability and Stakeholder Context: A citywide sustainability report was referenced, noting that 
Nashua had missed some 2025 goals related to greenhouse gas and urban trees. It was acknowledged 
that any tree work at Greeley Park is likely to face pushback from the Conservation Commission and 
Sustainability Committee, making careful communication critical. Alderman Klee will share this report 
with the Committee.
Approval Path: Any forestry management actions require BPW approval. The committee plans to prepare 
an agenda for the September BPW meeting focusing on forest floor cleanup and the need for a 
professional evaluation. 
Playground Repairs: A discussion was postponed. 
To Do Items for next Meeting: 
• Matt Sullivan will be invited to the September 9th Greeley Park Advisory Committee meeting to 
discuss the master plan RFP and funding. 
• Continue posting pool updates on the Parks and Rec webpage and DPW Facebook. 
• Install pool closure/reopening signs. 
• Alderwoman Klee to obtain and share the citywide sustainability report. 
• Prepare an agenda for the September BPW meeting focusing on forest floor cleanup and 
professional evaluation. 
• Stephanie Ballentine to contact UNH Cooperative Extension to explore their evaluation process, 
expertise, and cost. 
• Coordinate with DPW/BPW on involvement in any walkthroughs and confirm public notice 
requirements. 
• Develop educational messaging emphasizing forest health, safety, and an evaluation-first 
approach. 
• Kathi Lodi will compile Greeley Park's history and a copy of the will for the next meeting. 
• Contact Dan Hudson or Mark Sanders in the Engineering department to search for old park plans. 
• Lisa Law to speak with the historical society about historical documents and photos. 
• Discuss using the city website for the marketing campaign with Liz Hannah. 
• Start to explore setting up historical displays at City Hall and the library. 
Adjourned: 5:50pm 
 
Submitted August 18, 2026 
Stephanie Ballentine
